text:
The concept of relativity suggests that time is not absolute and can vary depending on speed and gravity. Imagine you're on a train moving close to the speed of light; for you, time feels normal, but for an observer outside the train, your clock would be ticking much slower.

To understand this better, think of time like a rubber band. When you are moving very fast or are in a strong gravitational field (like near a black hole), the rubber band stretches. For you, the "ticks" of your clock are still regular, but to someone watching from a distance, those ticks seem to happen more slowly because the rubber band of time has been stretched out.
